package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to and including Serv-U 15.4.2 HF 1
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of SolarWinds Serv-U contain a directory traversal vulnerability (CVE-2024-28995) that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read arbitrary files on the host system by sending specially crafted HTTP requests. This leads to information disclosure, exposure of sensitive system files, and enables further compromise of the server.

execution_context.file_location: web server file request handler (internal Serv-U code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the server receives a crafted HTTP GET request containing directory traversal sequences (../), the file handler resolves the path to a file outside the intended directory, and the server reads and returns the contents of the specified file (e.g., /etc/passwd) to the unauthenticated requester.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This HTTP request is crafted to exploit a directory traversal vulnerability, enabling access to files outside the permitted directory structure without authentication, which is a clear violation of security boundaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal file transfer or web server software should restrict file access to authorized directories and authenticated users. This behavior allows unauthenticated users to access any file on the system, bypassing all intended access controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate file requests are restricted to files within the user's permitted directory tree and never use ../ sequences to escape the root directory. Directory traversal patterns in file paths are not used in normal operation.
key_indicators: Presence of ../ or URL-encoded equivalents (%2e%2e%2f) in HTTP request paths
Requests targeting sensitive system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, Windows SAM, application config files)
Unauthenticated HTTP requests attempting to access files outside user home or allowed directories
Server responses containing contents of files not normally accessible via the web interface

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP GET request with directory traversal sequences (../) in the file path to the Serv-U server.
attack_chain.leads_to: The server resolves the path and returns the contents of arbitrary files, such as /etc/passwd, to the attacker.

attack_chain.action: Attacker collects sensitive information (such as credentials, configuration files, or other confidential data) from the exfiltrated files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker uses the stolen information to escalate privileges, gain further access, or pivot to other systems within the network.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP requests containing directory traversal patterns (../ or URL-encoded equivalents) in file paths
Unauthenticated requests for files located outside of user or application home directories
Access to sensitive system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, Windows SAM) via the web interface
Unusual file access patterns in web server logs, especially targeting system or configuration files
file_indicators: Access attempts to /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM, or application configuration files via HTTP requests
Web server log entries showing file paths with ../ or %2e%2e%2f sequences
Unexpected file reads or downloads of sensitive files from the Serv-U server
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with raw or URL-encoded directory traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e%2f) in the URL path
Unusual outbound HTTP responses containing the contents of sensitive files (e.g., lines matching passwd or SAM file formats)
Repeated requests from the same source IP for different sensitive files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web server logs for HTTP requests containing directory traversal patterns (../ or %2e%2e%2f) in file paths, especially those targeting sensitive files such as /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, or Windows SAM. Alert on unauthenticated requests that attempt to access files outside of permitted directories. Deploy web application firewalls (WAF) with rules to block or flag such requests. Review for large or unusual file downloads from the Serv-U server, and correlate with access logs for evidence of directory traversal attempts.
